**Surah al-ʿAṣr**

It is Makki according to Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn al-Zubayr and the majority of scholars, and Madani according to Mujahid, Qatadah and Muqatil. Its verses number three, without disagreement. Despite its brevity, it gathers a great deal of knowledge. It is related from al-Shafiʿi (may Allah have mercy on him) that he said: "Had only this surah been revealed, it would have sufficed people, for it encompasses all the sciences of the Qur'an."

Al-Tabarani in al-Awsat and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shuʿab transmitted from Abu Hudhayfah, who was a Companion, that he said: "When two men from among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) met, they would not part until one of them recited Surah 'al-ʿAṣr' to the other, and then one of them would greet the other with salam." It contains an allusion to the state of one whom the pursuit of worldly increase (al-takāthur) does not distract, and for this reason it was placed after Surah al-Takathur.

**In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.**

﴿By time﴾. Muqatil said: Allah, glorified is He, swore by the ʿAṣr prayer, because of its excellence, since according to the majority it is the Middle Prayer (al-Ṣalāt al-Wusṭā, the prayer in the middle), due to the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "They kept us busy from the Middle Prayer, the prayer of ʿAṣr."

And due to what is in the Mushaf of Hafsah: "And the Middle Prayer is the prayer of ʿAṣr."

And in a hadith: "Whoever misses the ʿAṣr prayer, it is as if he has lost his family and his wealth."

It is related that a woman used to cry out in the streets of Madinah: "Point me to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)!" He saw her and asked her: "What has happened?"

She said: "O Messenger of Allah, my husband was absent, so I committed fornication. Then a child was born to me from that fornication, so I threw the child into a jar of vinegar, and it died. Then I sold that vinegar. Is there any repentance for me?" He (ﷺ) said: "As for the fornication, upon you is stoning because of it. As for the killing, its recompense is Hell. As for selling the vinegar, you have committed a great sin. But I think you have abandoned the ʿAṣr prayer."

Al-Imam (al-Baghawi or another, as cited) mentioned it, and he, by my life, is an imam in transmitting such things, yet it is not relied upon by the imams of hadith. So beware of following him in this.

The prayer was singled out for excellence because performing it is more arduous, since people are preoccupied with their trades and livelihoods at the end of the day.

It was also said: Allah, mighty and majestic, swore by the time of that prayer because of its excellence, or because Adam, father of humankind (peace be upon him), was created at that time on Friday. Qatadah adopted this view; it is related from him that he said: "al-ʿAṣr is the evening (al-ʿashiyy). Allah, glorified is He, swore by it just as He swore by the forenoon (al-Ḍuḥā), because of the signs of power in both."

al-Zajjaj said: "al-ʿAṣr is the day, and al-ʿAṣr is the night." Upon this is the verse of Humayd ibn Thawr:

*And the two ʿaṣrs (day and night) did not tarry, when they sought to overtake what they had aimed at.*

It was also said: al-ʿAṣr is the early part of the day (bukrah) and the ʿAṣr is the evening (ʿashiyyah), and these are the two "cooling" times (al-Ibrādān). Upon this view, and upon what came before it, the oath is by one of the two matters, unspecified.

It was also said: the intended meaning is the era of Prophethood, as if He meant the time of his life (peace be upon him), as if it were the most noble of eras, to honour the Prophet (ﷺ).

It was also said: it is the time of his life (ﷺ) and what follows it until the Day of Resurrection. Its measure, in what has passed of time, is the measure of the time of ʿAṣr in the day. This is indicated by what al-Bukhari related from Salim ibn ʿAbd Allah, from his father, that he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Your remaining time, compared to the nations that came before you, is like the span between the ʿAṣr prayer and the setting of the sun."

Its nobility is due to its being the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his ummah, which is "the best nation brought forth for mankind." Its being later does not diminish it, just as the spearhead is not harmed by being behind the tip of its shaft, nor the blossom by being behind the tips of its branches.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is "the Dahr" (time, the ages), by which Allah, mighty and majestic, swore because it contains kinds of wonders. For this reason it is called "Abu al-ʿAjab" (father of wonder). Allah, mighty and majestic, by swearing by it, reminds of the blessings within it and their opposites, to alert the human being who is prepared for loss and for happiness. He, mighty and majestic, also indicates, through the oath by it, its glorification, by negating that it could have any loss or any role in it, as is claimed by those who attribute events to it. The attribution of loss to humankind after this indicates that it is a quality of humankind and not of time, as was said:

*They blame time, yet there is nothing in it of faults, except for people who are unworthy of time.*

And it has been objected that the use of "al-ʿAṣr" in this sense is not apparent.

Indeed, mankind is in loss (khusr).

That is, a loss in their trade and their endeavours, and in spending their lives on their aims, from which they gain nothing in the Hereafter; rather, these aims may even harm them when they arrive at the Sahirah (the wakeful plain of Resurrection).

The definite article in al-insan (ال) is for comprehensiveness (istighraq), as shown by the exception that follows in the surah. The indefinite noun khusr (خُسْرٍ) is said by some to be for magnification, meaning a great loss. It may also be for specification (tanwi') — that is, a kind of loss other than what man recognises.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 103, verse 3:

﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, for they are in a trade that will never fail, in that they have sold what is perishable and base and bought what is lasting and precious, and have exchanged the abiding righteous deeds for the passing and fleeting things. How excellent a bargain this is, how profitable, and what a benefit that gathers all good, how clear it is!

What is meant by the relative clause is everyone who is characterized by the description of the relative clause, not only ʿAli (may Allah ennoble his face) and Salman al-Farisi (may Allah be pleased with him) alone, as might be imagined from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with both of them) mentioning only them. Rather, both of them enter into this in the first instance. Similar to this is his restricting the losing human to Abu Jahl, which is evident. This is an explanation of their perfecting themselves.

And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿and they enjoin one another to the truth﴾ and so on is an explanation of their perfecting others,
Page 229
i.e., some of them enjoin others to the established matter which cannot be denied and which does not cease in both abodes because of its excellent effects, and it is all good: faith in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and following His books and His messengers, peace be upon them, in every belief and action.

﴿and they enjoin one another to patience﴾ regarding the sins that the soul longs for by the nature of human disposition, and upon the acts of obedience that are difficult for it to perform, and upon what Allah the Exalted tests His servants with of calamities. The patience mentioned is included in the truth, and it is mentioned after it with the repetition of the preposition and of the verb related to it, to show the complete care given to it. It is also possible that the first refers to the rank of worship, which is doing what pleases Allah the Exalted, and the second refers to the rank of servitude, which is contentment with what Allah the Exalted has done; for the meaning of patience is not merely restraining the soul from what it craves of action or abstention, but rather receiving what comes from Him, Mighty and Majestic, with beauty and being content with it, inwardly and outwardly.

Salam, Harun, and Ibn Musa recited from Abu ʿAmr: «wal-ʿaṣiri» with a kasra on the ṣad, and «waṣ-ṣabiri» with a kasra on the ba'. Ibn ʿAtiyya said: This is not permissible except in pausal form with transfer of the vowel (naql al-ḥaraka). It is also narrated from Abu ʿAmr «bi-ṣ-ṣabiri» with a kasra on the ba' as ishmam (a partial, lip-rounded vowel). This, as he said, also occurs only in pause. The author of al-Lawami said: ʿIsa of Basra recited «bis-ṣabir» by transferring the vowel of the rāʾ to the bāʾ, so that one need not give a partial vowel in pause nor pronounce a sukun that would bring together two unvocalized letters. This is a widespread dialect, not an anomalous one, but a well-known one; it indicates the case ending (iʿrab), separates from the meeting of two sakins, and fulfills the right of the word on which one pauses regarding its sukun, end quote.

From this, as in al-Bahr, is his saying:

I am Jarir, my kunya is Abu ʿAmr, I strike with the sword, and Saʿd is in al-ʿaṣir.

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and others narrated from ʿAli (may Allah ennoble his face) that he used to recite:

«Wal-ʿaṣri wa-nawaʾib id-dahri, inna l-insana lafi khusrin, wa-innahu lafihi ila akhiri d-dahri.»

ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Dawud in al-Masahif narrated from Maymun ibn Mihran that he recited: «Wal-ʿaṣri, inna l-insana lafi khusrin, wa-innahu lafihi ila akhiri d-dahri, illa lladhina amanu.» He mentioned that this is the recitation of Ibn Masʿud. This is the end of that.

Some of the Mu'tazila used what is in this surah to argue that the perpetrator of a major sin is eternal in the Fire, because it made no exception from loss except those who believe and do righteous deeds, etc. It was answered that there is no indication in that beyond the fact that the non-excepted are in loss, and as for their being eternal in the Fire, there is no indication of that whatsoever. The loss is general: it is either by eternity if he dies as a disbeliever, or by entering the Fire if he dies as a disobedient, and by missing the lofty ranks if He forgives him. This is a good answer. Imam al-Maturidi, may Allah have mercy on him, had elaborate efforts in investigating this matter, mentioned in at-Ta'wilat, so do not be heedless. And in the surah is an exhortation to enjoining good and forbidding evil, and that a person should love for his brother what he loves for himself, which is not hidden.
